outsiders.name: Matt Jarbo
outsiders.text:
Apparently David Fincher used generative AI in THE FURTHER MIS-ADVENTURES OF CLIFF BOOTH, and somehow that's made me MORE interested in seeing it.

Next Best Picture calls the AI an "eyesore," but doesn't identify a single scene or explain how they determined it was AI. And despite that criticism, the reviewer still gave the movie a 7/10.

Netflix just spent $587 MILLION buying Ben Affleck's AI filmmaking company, InterPositive. I don't know if that technology was used here, but I'm genuinely curious how someone as meticulous as Fincher might incorporate generative AI into recreating 1970s Hollywood, especially following Tarantino's love letter to that era.

If the effects look like shit, criticize them! That's completely fair. But remember when CGI was so obvious you could spot it a mile away? Now it's everywhere, and half the time nobody notices.

I'd rather see what Fincher actually did before joining another round of AI panic.

outsiders.draft_en:
So David Fincher reportedly put generative AI into his new one, The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth. Weirdly, that makes me want to see it more.

Next Best Picture called the AI an "eyesore" yet never pointed to a scene or said how they could tell - and still scored the film 7/10.

Netflix also just paid $587 MILLION for InterPositive, the AI filmmaking company Ben Affleck started. No idea if that tech is in here, but I want to know how a director as precise as Fincher would use generative AI to rebuild 1970s Hollywood, right after Tarantino's own tribute to that era.

Bad effects deserve criticism, fair enough. But CGI used to stick out a mile away, and now it is everywhere and mostly invisible.

I will wait to see what Fincher really did before signing up for the next wave of AI panic.

virals.name: Matt Jarbo
virals.text:
Apparently David Fincher used generative AI in THE FURTHER MIS-ADVENTURES OF CLIFF BOOTH, and somehow that's made me MORE interested in seeing it.

Next Best Picture calls the AI an "eyesore," but doesn't identify a single scene or explain how they determined it was AI. And despite that criticism, the reviewer still gave the movie a 7/10.

Netflix just spent $587 MILLION buying Ben Affleck's AI filmmaking company, InterPositive. I don't know if that technology was used here, but I'm genuinely curious how someone as meticulous as Fincher might incorporate generative AI into recreating 1970s Hollywood, especially following Tarantino's love letter to that era.

If the effects look like shit, criticize them! That's completely fair. But remember when CGI was so obvious you could spot it a mile away? Now it's everywhere, and half the time nobody notices.

I'd rather see what Fincher actually did before joining another round of AI panic.
